display.title: Simchah Shel Mitzvah: The Joy of Being Connected to Hashem
display.summary_short: A class on the joy of mitzvos: a Hayom Yom on what 'mitzvah' means, and a sichah of the Rebbe comparing two kinds of joy to the wine and water poured on the Mizbeach.
display.summary_long: The teacher opens the class by giving thanks: two years earlier on this day he was critically ill with COVID and Hashem brought him through. The class then studies the Hayom Yom of 8 Cheshvan: 'mitzvah' comes from 'tzavsa', joining, so every mitzvah connects the one who does it with Hashem, the One who commands it, and that connection is itself the reward. The Frierdiker Rebbe's parable of a great scholar who asks a simple man for a favor shows how a command makes the simple man important and binds the two together, whether the task is large or small. The teacher tells how the Rebbe told a bar mitzvah boy that every brachah, 'Blessed are You', is a meeting with the King, and explains why our whole day, even Shabbos meals, becomes holy. The second text is a sichah of the Rebbe: wine poured on the Mizbeach stands for a joy we understand and taste, still limited and tied to ourselves; water, which has no taste, stands for the boundless joy of doing what Hashem wants simply because He commanded it. Along the way the teacher shares childhood memories of seeing the Rebbe.
display.lesson: Every mitzvah, large or small, connects us to Hashem, and the deepest joy comes from doing His will simply because He commanded it.

other_personal.text: The teacher was the first Crown Heights patient hospitalized for COVID; on 26 Adar 5780 doctors did not expect him to survive the day.

As a small child his family lived on the second floor of the President St and New York Ave building where the Rebbe and Rebbetzin lived; he attended a kindergarten next door to the Rebbe's later house.
